speaker: expecting_mother
quote: most nights i don’t sleep until 4-8 am because i am waiting to be exhausted to a point the pain no longer matters. i find myself laying on my back often, i know it’s bad but it’s the only position that brings me any relief even if for a bit, i don’t know what to do. i’ve tried using pregnancy pillows and they didn’t help
context: At 23 weeks, side sleeping painful; pillows haven't helped.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: the guilt comes from if something goes wrong i know i will be at fault just because i thought sleeping on my back is more comfortable and it scares me
context: Why she feels guilty about her sleep position.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: When it comes to our baby, he was very supportive in the beginning and would buy the things I needed. But recently, I can’t shake the feeling that I’ve become more of a burden or an obligation to him rather than a partner he’s excited to build a life with.
context: At 12 weeks, planning a wedding before the due date mostly alone.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: I feel like healing from a c-section while also caring for a toddler too is going to be a lot rougher than the first go around. So I’m curious, if you had a choice what would you choose? Has anyone had a c-section while caring for a toddler?
context: Second pregnancy, offered a choice of birth mode after a first surgical birth.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: previous to finding out I was pregnant, I had some A/L booked off work but I’m back in tomorrow and dreading it. I work in healthcare, and though not clinical anymore I do regularly go on wards and health centres for long periods of time where I don’t always know where the loos are
context: UK, 5+4 weeks, first pregnancy, sick early and facing a return to work.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I’m finding so this so difficult already, and I’m not even in those ‘peak weeks’ where everyone says it’s the worst
context: Already struggling at 5 weeks before the weeks she's been told are the worst.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: Managed to get a GP appointment tonight after being sent home from work this morning, really is a miserable feeling!
context: The next day, sent home from her healthcare job.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: This time he called my mom to come sit with me, which I appreciate, but I feel like he’s missing the point. I don’t just need someone here—I want my husband here.
context: Four months after a birth, newly pregnant again, her husband out with friends and family.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I’m already getting comments from grandparents (on both sides) how they are taking off work and going to be over all the time the month baby is born as well as be waiting in waiting room when baby arrives, it’s honestly giving me a lot of anxiety
context: First pregnancy, second trimester, grandparents announcing their own plans for the birth month.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I don’t know what I want yet, but I don’t like that they’re already telling me what they’re going to do and not asking
context: She hasn't decided her own visitor plan yet.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I’m sure the help will be great, but I’m just scared I’m going to be overwhelmed and just want to be alone with my baby, especially that first month.
context: Her fear about the grandparents' plans for the first month.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: we have several friends who have been TTC for years and I feel guilty announcing (publicly or privately). How do I tell them without feeling/being selfish and shallow?
context: Newly pregnant with her second child.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: FTM here, and I feel like I know absolutely nothing about babies! How to care for them, when to feed them, recognizing their cues, diaper changes…you name it.
context: First pregnancy, due in November, wanting to learn newborn care.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: Does anyone have any online classes, videos, courses, or resources that really helped them learn how to care for a newborn after birth?
context: Asking for paid or free newborn-care resources.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: My 2 y/o is impulsive and is so difficult to redirect. I get it - typical toddler behavior. But with a crying newborn on top of getting kicked and constantly touched, I am so over it.
context: Four weeks after her second birth, with a two-year-old.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: And my pelvic floor is just so weak. I feel like I can feel it even more now and I feel so defeated.
context: Four weeks after her second birth.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I have a HUGE fear of IVs, epidurals, spinal taps, and catheters
context: 12 weeks, her hospital doesn't offer the gas she hoped to use instead of an epidural.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: There’s an alternative birthing center I could use, but it’s over an hour away and I’m already pushing it with my time off of work for appointments (I’m salaried and have “unlimited” vacation that is subject to court of public opinion so I can’t just take unpaid time off)
context: Weighing a farther birth centre against time off work for appointments.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: They have been okay so far but not super attentive and said there’s a “baby boom” so they are filled to the brim.
context: At 12 weeks, her local hospital 30 minutes away.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: I’ve considered toddler boards or an attachable seat that I’ve seen some ads for. We have a nuna mixx next pram that was gifted to us and we can’t afford the nuna toddler board but not sure if a universal one would work well with this pram.
context: Due any day with her second, planning outings with a two-year-old.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: If I go anywhere without putting our 2 year old in the pram I regret in within about 15 mins
context: Why she wants the toddler in the pram with the newborn.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I’m honestly terrified to give birth, and not just that but I’m feeling overwhelmed with what to do after the birth. I honestly have no idea what the heck I’m doing. How do I know how often a baby needs to eat?? How do I know if he’s too hot or too cold?
context: First pregnancy, 32 weeks, nerves rising.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: My whole summer just feels like a countdown till baby boy is here, and then recovering from birth.
context: 32 weeks in early June, uncomfortable and physically limited.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: If for some reason I need to go to hospital, I would have no idea where to start with the medical care in Vietnam, I already struggle enough to navigate it all in Australia
context: Australia, 7 weeks, first pregnancy, weighing a destination wedding as bridesmaid.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I was absolutely fine to go without him before we found out I was pregnant, but I’m simply not comfortable being away from him at a vulnerable point in my life especially considering it’s my first time.
context: Her husband can't come to the overseas wedding.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: closer to labour i am needing more things pads, underwear, tens machine, pyjamas, stuff for hospital.
context: UK, deciding which birth and postpartum items come from the joint account.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: There is a part of me though who thinks why do I have to absorb the cost of needing different clothes to accomplish my pregnant then postpartum/nursing body.
context: Maternity clothes and bras bought on her own card.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: It's partly my fault because I skated through my wonderful pregnancy with the mindset of "I'll just get an epidural" thinking Id avoid the worst of it. I was not prepared for how much pain there would be.
context: Six years after a first birth she calls traumatic, preparing for a second.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: Called the hospital around 3am. They told me to wait until contractions were 5 min apart for 2 hours.
context: First pregnancy, 39+2, logging days of on-off contractions; later sent home at 1 cm.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: Are we talking hours, days, or "see you at 41 weeks"?
context: After being sent home from hospital in early labour.
